text:
zoe: hi all, new hire here — VPN connected but can't pull docker images from our internal registry (10.40.12.7). `docker pull` fails with timeout. anyone seen this during first-day setup?

rahul: welcome! quick checks: are you on the company image? what client shows (split/full)? also paste output of `scutil --dns` and `netstat -rn` if you can.

zoe: company laptop (macbook air m2), our-agent v2.3, says split-tunnel. netstat shows:
```
default 192.168.10.1 en0
10.40.0.0/16 192.168.10.1 en0   <-- suspicious
172.23.55.0/24 172.23.55.1 utun3
```
DNS has both 8.8.8.8 and 172.23.55.10.

rahul: yep 10.40/16 route is going to your home router. two quick fixes: (1) add a route via the VPN gw: `sudo route -n add -net 10.40.0.0/16 172.23.55.1` or (2) temporarily tether to phone hotspot and re-initiate the VPN so client can push correct routes.

zoe: doing the route add now... `sudo route -n add -net 10.40.0.0/16 172.23.55.1` -> worked. `docker pull` now progressing. thanks! :relieved: 

naya: small FYI — we saw a batch of M1 Macbooks where our-agent skips route push when LAN matches 10.40/16. infra is tracking. If you want persistence, i can DM you a `~/Library/LaunchAgents` plist snippet to reapply at login.

ops-bot: Created ticket INFRA-4682: "split-tunnel route conflict on macOS M1 - 10.40/16 not applied when LAN overlaps" assigned to @naya.

helpdesk-bot: If you still hit issues, open a support request at https://support.redwood.internal and include `netstat -rn` output and client logs from `~/Library/Logs/redwood-agent/`.

zoe: awesome, thanks everyone. ping me the plist when you have a sec, naya. saved my first pairing session :)
